answer: Each earning key posts a bond and receives a uniquely faceted onyx token, bevel map filed at signup. When the registry names a random start minute, only that holder may wander a measured city circuit and arrive at the assay bench in time, seating the token against a catalogued prism so the polished face yields a line pattern matching the filed map and transit residual. A copied stone fails the facet spectrum; one walker cannot finish two circuits in the same window, and the bond burns. N aliases therefore cost N distinct onyx cuttings and N attendants on the road at once.
